items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Udell Wilson, Inez Trepani on drum, a boy called Georgie Boy, a clarinet, they're all dead now. All but Manuel.

ctx.x: Oh, I heard, yeah, Manuel Moneta talking about it. And Manuel Moneta was in the band.
Udell Wilson, Inez Trepani on drum, a boy called Georgie Boy, a clarinet, they're all dead now. All but Manuel. Manuel looked fine last time I said it.
Well he said to tell everybody how low for him too. Yeah, they look good, Manuel did. He's pretty heavy, but he's good health though.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-21
items.q: And they had Lee Collin on trumpet.

ctx.x: Near the clarinet. George Field. See, I get Papa. See, I get Papa. George Field. We played and played and played. The arrangement was made. Randy. After Parker Brothers, John Daniels, John Daniels, Harry Brooks and Kit Harris. They were his friends from New York. They know each other as well. Well, they spoke at Harry Parker. He had his bartender at the 101 Ranch with Jew Morris. And a great friend to Billy Phillip. So, they said, Why don't you give Billy the preference? All right. Tell Billy about it. Jew Morris…

A fine gentleman. Came down to make the arrangement. He buys the place, 101 Ranch. I heard him speak over conversations. No oppositions. Taking my girls out of here, over to your place. Come to the agreement. No oppositions. Well, they ran. Barely opened up. They had Fair Bear Ridley. Dave Argan on drums. And they had Lee Collin on trumpet. And they had one of my old players I had in my band in Camp Pike. Georgia Boyd on Clannett. Well, they ran. Everything ran all right. Until the Easter comes on. On Easter…
Who was being shot? Who was being shot? Who was shot? Who all was shot?
